column2: “🧭 Find”: what does “Found in the text” show, and how do I add it to a record?
column3: After “🧭 Find”, the workshop shows one card per person with what the text says about them: age (and estimated birth “about 1787” if the date of the record is known), occupation, origin, birthplace, residence, relationship (brother, son of, widow of…), role and status; each field can be ticked or unticked. Variants of the same name (“Jemielet” / “Jemichet”) are grouped, false names (“Cafins de”, “BTIS”) are set aside, and the records in your database that look alike are suggested. Then come the sections 📍 Places, 📅 Dates (even written in words or in the republican calendar), 🎂 Ages, ⚔️ Events and context (a battle, prisoners… linked to “🌍 The world around” if it knows it), 📜 Kind of record (only suggested) and 🔢 Numbers. On every item, “＋ Add to a record…” (also through “⋯” or a right-click): you choose the record, then “as what” (event, note, occupation, residence or info), with a preview; the source (this document, the line) and the sentence as a quote are always attached, and “↶ Undo” reverses the addition. If in-depth reading is installed, “🔍 Find with the AI” sends only the text to the model on your computer; its suggestions are marked 🔍 AI. ⚙️ sets the sections shown and the AI (suggest, automatic or never).
